For the triangle above, find $m∠M$ in degrees to two decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $M:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{n}^{2}+{l}^{2}-{m}^{2}}{2nl}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Here, we have

$$
m=29,\,n=20,\,l=13.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡M & =\frac{{20}^{2}+{13}^{2}-{29}^{2}}{2(20)(13)} \\  & =\frac{400+169-841}{520} \\  & =\frac{-272}{520} \\  & =\frac{-34}{65}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠M & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(-\frac{34}{65}) \\  & ={121.54}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
